subject: Packaging flexibility and downgrade path — Luminary Health
messages:
From: Elena Smith <elena.smith@luminaryhealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T10:12:00Z
Subject: Packaging options and potential downgrade for Luminary Health

Hi Vanessa,

Quick summary: we're evaluating a move from Pro to Standard for a subset of workloads to reduce spend for Q1. We still need burst/dedicated capacity for our latency-sensitive endpoints (clinical triage) but can tolerate reduced seats elsewhere.

Questions:
- Can we retain Dedicated capacity for a single route while downgrading the rest to Standard?
- What does feature bundling look like (monitoring, alerting, higher retention) if we move down tiers?
- Any pro-rated credits / rollback terms if we see a regression in Q1?

Attached our current contract for reference. Would like annotated pricing scenarios and a recommended rollback checklist.

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Platform Operations
Luminary Health
[Attachment: current_contract.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Smith <elena.smith@luminaryhealth.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Packaging options and potential downgrade for Luminary Health

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the contract. Short answer: yes, we can do a hybrid downgrade with a preserved Dedicated pool for critical routes. Below I laid out three scenarios with practical tradeoffs.

1) Minimal-risk hybrid (recommended)
- Keep current Dedicated for clinical-triage route only.
- Downgrade remaining capacity to Standard; apply 30% token discount on Standard for committed monthly usage threshold.
- Keep monitoring & alerting as an add-on bundle (monthly charge).
- Rollback: 7-day ramp window with a one-time re-provisioning fee (estimated $1,200).

2) Cost-first downgrade
- Move all routing to Standard; reserve burst pool for emergencies only.
- Lower monthly cost (~18% savings) but higher tail latency during peak.
- Monitoring downgraded to 14-day retention.

3) 12-month commitment (safest economics)
- 12-month term, 10% standard discount + option to upgrade routes quarterly without re-provisioning fee.
- We can include a 30-day rollback SLA for the first quarter.

I've attached an initial pricing workbook with per-scenario numbers and a short rollback checklist. If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the numbers and sign an addendum.

Proposed next step: 30-minute review + agreement on which routes are "critical" and candidate rollback metrics (latency P95, error-rate).

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Packaging options and potential downgrade for Luminary Health — approval request

Team — looping you in for pricing/credit approval. Luminary (deal RD-2026-1197) is asking for: hybrid downgrade (Dedicated preserved for one route), 12-month optional commit path, and an explicit rollback clause with a re-provisioning window.

Ask: approval for a one-time concession (if they sign 12 months) of up to 15% on the first-quarter invoice OR a re-provisioning fee waiver. We can trade that for a signed 12-month commitment and a 30-day rollback window.

Key points:
- ARR impact if they take cost-first downgrade vs hybrid: estimated -$52k / year.
- If they commit 12mo with concession, net ARR delta is -$12k / year but reduces churn risk.
- Need legal to sign a short addendum; I'd prefer to push DocuSign link rather than manual redlines.

Any objections to approving up to 15% concession or should we cap at 10% and include a stricter rollback clause?

—Vanessa

From: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T11:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Packaging options and potential downgrade for Luminary Health — approval request

Vanessa — reviewed. Approve a 10% concession on the first invoice (upfront credit) if Luminary signs a 12-month commitment. No more than 10% without Director approval. Make sure the addendum includes:
- 30-day rollback clause limited to three rollback windows in the 12-month term
- Re-provisioning SLA and cost caps (we should not waive all fees)
- Performance metrics that trigger rollback (P95 latency > X ms or error-rate > Y%)

Include me on the DocuSign envelope. I'll also attach an approval memo.

Thanks — S.
[Attachment: approved_discount_term.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]
